why: With parent pointers, the ancestors of a node form a single path to the root, so the LCA is the first node where p's root path and q's root path meet. Mark p's path, then climb from q until you land on a marked node.
hints: From any node, following parent[] gives exactly one path to the root. What are the common ancestors of p and q in terms of those two paths?
The common ancestors are the shared tail of the two root paths; the lowest one is the first shared node you reach climbing from q.
Put every node on p's root path into a set, then walk q upward until it is in the set. O(depth) time and space, at most O(n).
pitfalls: A node is its own ancestor: if p is an ancestor of q, the answer is p.
Use iteration, not recursion: a chain of 100,000 nodes is possible.
